categories.name: Physical & Built Environment
categories.intro: The tangible world the organization manages. The defining modelling challenge in this category is time: retail space is reconfigured continuously, so physical concepts must be effective-dated to keep historical performance comparable.

concepts.name: Land (Site)
concepts.definition: The contiguous or functionally unified physical ground area on which a property is situated, representing the site as a whole regardless of how many cadastral parcels it comprises.
concepts.characteristics: Aggregates one or more Land Parcels into a single managed site identity; stable across parcel boundary changes or additions; the spatial context for the property asset. change1
concepts.standardsNote:
ISO 19152 (LADM): Published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) under Technical Committee ISO/TC 211, the Land Administration Domain Model has been substantially updated and is now a multi-part series; the current foundational document is ISO 19152-1:2024, "Geographic information — Land Administration Domain Model (LADM) — Part 1: Generic conceptual model," which provides an abstract, encoding-independent conceptual model covering parties, spatial units (including parcels), and legal rights, responsibilities, and restrictions, with refined support for versioning and temporal modelling. The Spatial Units package is the part most directly relevant to the "Land (Site)" concept, as it formalizes how a plot of ground — potentially comprising multiple cadastral parcels — can be described as a coherent administrative unit independently of any particular registration boundary. This justifies the citation because the model supplies the conceptual precedent for treating a functionally unified site as a single identifiable object that may aggregate several underlying parcels, which is precisely the distinction the "Land (Site)" concept makes. The standard is available from ISO at https://www.iso.org/standard/81263.html; the original 2012 edition (ISO 19152:2012) remains catalogued at https://www.iso.org/standard/51206.html.



MSCI/IPD asset-level reporting: MSCI (formerly IPD, which MSCI acquired in 2012) publishes the "MSCI Global Data Standards for Real Estate Investment," the most current edition dated April 2026 and available at https://www.msci.com/documents/1296102/1672393/MSCI+Global+Data+Standards+for+Real+Estate+Investment.pdf. The document establishes a common framework for measuring and reporting the performance and risk of private real estate investments at the vehicle, asset, and tenancy levels, and it explicitly addresses the lack of consistent global data standards as a problem that prevents meaningful cross-market comparison. It is relevant to the "Land (Site)" concept because the standards treat each directly held property as a discrete, individually measured asset — requiring that physical attributes such as floor area and location be attributed to a single asset record — which necessitates a well-defined notion of the site as the ground-level unit of investment, irrespective of how many cadastral parcels underlie it. Methodology documents, including the "MSCI Global Methodology Standards for Real Estate Investment" and the "MSCI Property Indexes Methodology," are accessible from the MSCI Real Estate Methodology Documents page at https://www.msci.com/real-estate-methodology.

concepts.name: Property
concepts.definition: The shopping centre as a distinct physical and legal object: land and buildings together with the rights held over them.
concepts.characteristics: Lifecycle states (development, operational, refurbishment, divestment); format classification; GLA vs GBA reconciliation; anchor of most performance aggregation. 'Asset' names a role, not the thing: the portfolio role is expressed through Ownership & Fund Structure and Valuation, the accounting representation through Fixed Asset, and the equipment view through Technical Equipment.
concepts.standardsNote:
ICSC format definitions: 
ICSC (formerly the International Council of Shopping Centers, now doing business simply as ICSC) is the global trade association for what it terms the "Marketplaces Industry," covering shopping centers, malls, and all other retail real estate.
 
ICSC publishes a standardized classification of shopping centers based on size and characteristics,
 
defining a shopping center as a group of retail and commercial establishments that is planned, developed, owned, and managed as a single property
 — a definition that directly grounds the concept of Property (Asset) as a bounded, managed entity with a stable identity. This citation is justified because the ICSC format definitions are the retail real estate industry's authoritative reference for what constitutes a distinct property, how its type is determined, and how its gross leasable area is characterized, all of which are preconditions for treating it as a valued asset. The regional classification standards can be verified through ICSC's website at icsc.com; the U.S. version is available directly at https://www.icsc.com/uploads/t07-subpage/US-Shopping-Center-Definition-Standard.pdf, under the heading "U.S. Shopping-Center Classification and Characteristics."

IPMS: 
As real estate markets become increasingly global, the need for international consistency in property measurement has grown correspondingly; historically, measurement practices were highly localized and lacked the transparency a global marketplace requires, which is why the International Property Measurement Standards were developed by a coalition of more than 80 property organizations and drafted by an independent group of 18 experts from 11 countries.
 
The IPMSC previously published asset-class-specific standards including IPMS: Retail Buildings (2019), and in 2023 combined all of these into the single consolidated IPMS: All Buildings,
 which establishes a hierarchy of measurement levels — from total external footprint through to exclusive occupier area — that underpins the model's requirement that every measurement carries a defined scope, source, and quality status. The citation is justified because IPMS provides the internationally recognized measurement framework that gives physical substance and comparability to a property's spatial definition across its lifecycle. 
The current standard, IPMS: All Buildings, is published by the International Property Measurement Standards Coalition (IPMSC)
 and is available for download at https://ipmsc.org/standards/; the document is structured in Parts A through G, with the measurement standards themselves in Part E.

ISO 55000: 
ISO 55000 is the foundational part of the ISO 55000 series on asset management, providing the overview, terminology, and principles necessary to develop a proactive asset management system, and it establishes the framework for organizations to manage their assets over their full lifecycles in order to enhance the value realized from those assets.
 
ISO 55000 describes the core concepts and benefits of asset management, and the 2024 edition reflects the evolution of the discipline since 2014 with a stronger focus on the outcomes of asset management activities.
 The citation is justified because the standard's treatment of an asset as something with potential or actual value to an organization — managed systematically across its lifecycle — is precisely the framing that the concept "Property (Asset)" adopts; ISO 55000 gives that framing international, cross-sector authority and supplies the vocabulary for governance, performance, risk, and value realization that an enterprise information model must anchor to. 
The current editions are ISO 55000:2024 (Asset management — Vocabulary, overview and principles) and ISO 55001:2024 (Asset management — Asset management system — Requirements),
 published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO); ISO 55000:2024 can be verified and purchased at https://www.iso.org/standard/83053.html.

concepts.name: Building
concepts.definition: A physical structure within a property, composed of floors and technical systems.
concepts.characteristics: Construction attributes; measurement basis for gross areas; handover documentation from construction projects.
concepts.standardsNote:
IPMS 1/2: The International Property Measurement Standards Coalition published IPMS: All Buildings in January 2023, consolidating all prior asset-class-specific standards into a single harmonised document.
 
Within that framework, IPMS 1 and IPMS 2 define external and internal measurements respectively for the whole or part of a building.
 
The standard establishes a levelled floor-by-floor measurement convention, designating the ground-level entrance as Level 0, with floors above numbered upward and floors below numbered downward,
 directly grounding the information model's definition of a building as a structure composed of floors. 
Component Areas are horizontal areas within a building designated according to their structure and function, with the sum of all Component Areas equalling the IPMS 1 figure for the building or level being measured,
 providing the normative basis for decomposing a building into measurable floor-level units. The standard is published by the International Property Measurement Standards Coalition (IPMSC); the current consolidated edition is titled "International Property Measurement Standards: All Buildings" (January 2023) and is freely available at https://ipmsc.org/standards/.


IFC (ISO 16739): The Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) constitute a standardised digital description of the built environment, published as an open, vendor-neutral international standard under ISO 16739-1:2024 by both buildingSMART International and the International Organization for Standardization.
 
The IFC schema models buildings via the IfcBuilding entity, which sits within a hierarchical spatial structure that decomposes a building into storeys (IfcBuildingStorey) and further into spaces (IfcSpace),
 directly mirroring the information model's definition of a building as composed of floors. 
Building service or electrical distribution systems, zonal systems, and structural analysis systems are also related to the building storeys through formal schema relationships,
 confirming the standard's coverage of the technical systems component of the concept. The current version is IFC 4.3 (ISO 16739-1:2024), maintained by buildingSMART International; the schema documentation is available at https://www.buildingsmart.org/standards/bsi-standards/industry-foundation-classes/, and the ISO publication is at https://www.iso.org/standard/84123.html.


COBie: The Construction-Operations Building Information Exchange (COBie) specification provides a standard organisation of data used to manage and maintain facility assets; it encompasses all space, product, and equipment schedules drawn from design drawings as well as as-built, operations and maintenance, and commissioning information captured during construction.
 
The COBie format is a subset of a Building Information Model, defined as a Model View Definition of the IFC schema,
 and its Facility, Floor, Space, and Component tables map directly onto the information model's concept of a building structured by floors and containing technical systems. 
Originally published by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in 2007, COBie has since been curated and maintained by the National Institute of Building Sciences (NIBS) under a Creative Commons licence;
 
version 2.4 was adopted within NBIMS-US V3 in 2015, and version 3 is the current release, forming part of NBIMS-US V4.
 The COBie V3 specification is available through NIBS at https://nibs.org/nbims/v3/cobie.

concepts.name: Floor / Zone
concepts.definition: Vertical (level) and horizontal (zone) subdivision of a building used for navigation, analysis and allocation.
concepts.characteristics: Zones often defined for footfall and leasing analysis rather than construction; both hierarchies must coexist.
concepts.standardsNote:
IPMS Component Areas: The International Property Measurement Standards (IPMS), published by the International Property Measurement Standards Coalition (IPMSC) and consolidated into the single harmonised document IPMS: All Buildings in January 2023, establishes a structured framework for decomposing floor area within a building into discrete, typed component areas — covering vertical elements, penetrations, circulation, primary use space, and shared facilities — measured level by level throughout the building. 
The standard requires that the sum of all component areas equal IPMS 1 for the building or for a given level of a building being measured
, which means every floor (vertical level) must be fully and exhaustively partitioned into named horizontal zones before any area figure can be reported. 
Because IPMS: All Buildings applies to all building types regardless of use or occupation, and carries the flexibility to measure only part of a building or to holistically measure all areas and allocate them into separate components
, the standard directly justifies treating Floor/Zone as a first-class model concept that combines both the vertical dimension (discrete numbered levels) and the horizontal dimension (typed area zones) of physical space. The standard can be verified at the IPMSC website (publisher: International Property Measurement Standards Coalition, document: IPMS: All Buildings, 2023, Part C — Measurement Practice and Component Areas): https://ipmsc.org/standards/

concepts.name: Media & Specialty Leasing Unit
concepts.definition: A lettable position for media, promotion or temporary retail — advertising surfaces, kiosks, pop-up sites — typically in common areas.
concepts.characteristics: High-volume, short-cycle letting; positions are defined by location and visibility rather than enclosed area; inventory management resembles media booking more than space letting.

concepts.name: Common Area
concepts.definition: Non-lettable shared space (malls, atria, restrooms, service corridors).
concepts.characteristics: Drives service charge allocation; explains the GLA/GBA gap; may host specialty leasing (kiosks, media).

concepts.name: Service Area
concepts.definition: A typed subdivision of a building's gross area that is neither lettable nor open to the general public as a common area, encompassing back-of-house, service corridors, plant rooms, loading bays and landlord-retained technical spaces; distinguished from Common Area by its access restriction and from Space by its non-lettable character.
concepts.characteristics: Access-controlled and restricted to authorised personnel or tenants; carries an area measurement on a declared basis (GIA/IPMS component) with effective dates; typed by function (service, plant, circulation, loading, landlord office) to support GLA/GFA reconciliation
concepts.standards: IPMS 1–3 (RICS/IASB, 2016 & 2021 revision) distinguishes Internal Dominated Areas including plant, service and circulation; BOMA 2017 Office/Retail Standard defines Service Areas and Floor Common Areas separately from Usable area; RICS Code of Measuring Practice 6th ed. distinguishes GIA components including service areas

concepts.name: Technical Equipment
concepts.definition: Maintainable equipment: escalators, HVAC, meters, access systems.
concepts.characteristics: Asset registry with criticality and maintenance regime; meters link consumption to spaces; classification via construction taxonomies.

concepts.name: Land Parcel
concepts.definition: A single cadastral unit of land with its own registered legal identifier, boundary survey and title record, forming the legally indivisible building block of a site.
concepts.characteristics: Uniquely identified by cadastral or title register reference; carries registered rights, encumbrances and ownership interests; one or more parcels aggregate to form a Land (Site)
concepts.standards: ISO 19152 (LADM); national land registry standards (e.g. HM Land Registry, Grundbuch, Kadaster)

concepts.name: Parking & Mobility Facility
concepts.definition: Parking structures and mobility infrastructure (car parks, EV charging, cycle facilities, logistics access) serving the property.
concepts.characteristics: Capacity and utilization are measurable; increasingly revenue-bearing (paid parking, EV charging) and ESG-relevant; may be shared with or operated by third parties.

concepts.name: Area Measurement
concepts.definition: A measured area figure for a space, building or property, stated on a declared basis at a point in time.
concepts.characteristics: Value plus basis, date and status — GLA, GBA and letting-plan areas are instances, not attributes; re-measurement creates a new record rather than overwriting; discrepancies between bases are first-class facts.
concepts.standardsNote:
IPMS: 
The International Property Measurement Standards are published by the International Property Measurement Standards Coalition (IPMSC), a body comprising over 80 professional and not-for-profit organisations from 11 countries.
 
The current version, IPMS: All Buildings, was published in January 2023 and consolidates all previously separate asset-class standards into a single harmonised framework applicable to every building type, regardless of use or occupation — including retail.
 It directly justifies the citation because 
it defines multiple area components and measurement levels with sufficient flexibility to capture different purposes, while adopting distinct nomenclature to avoid the inconsistencies found in localised market standards
 — precisely what an enterprise model needs when recording a measured area figure on a declared basis. Verification: International Property Measurement Standards Coalition (IPMSC), "IPMS: All Buildings" (2023), Parts B–E; available at https://ipmsc.org/standards/.

SS 21054: 
SS 21054:2020, titled "Area and volume of buildings — Terminology and measurement," is a Swedish standard published by the Swedish Institute for Standards (SIS).
 
It is used by area surveyors, architects, estate agents, and building planners, and is explicitly applicable to building permit processes, valuation, rent-setting, and property management
 — all contexts in which a shopping-mall operator in Sweden would need to declare a measured area figure against a recognised basis. 
This 2020 edition supersedes SS 21054:2009 edition 1
 and is the authoritative local standard that governs how Swedish floor areas are defined and calculated, making it the natural citation anchor for any Area Measurement concept applied to Swedish assets. Verification: Swedish Institute for Standards (SIS), "SS 21054:2020 Area and volume of buildings — Terminology and measurement," available at https://www.sis.se/en/produkter/construction-materials-and-building/buildings/general/ss-210542020/.

BOMA: 
BOMA International serves as the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) secretariat for a suite of area measurement standards
, giving its methods formal national-standards status in the United States. 
The current retail-specific instrument is BOMA 2025 for Retail Properties: Standard Method of Measurement (ANSI/BOMA Z65.5-2025), which is intended exclusively for retail properties and may be applied to single-tenant, multi-tenant, or multi-building configurations
 — directly relevant to shopping-mall measurement. 
Its primary objectives include promoting an unambiguous framework for determining rentable area, facilitating transparency among all commercial real estate participants, and aligning concepts with the International Property Measurement Standards
, which confirms why it belongs alongside IPMS as a complementary citation for any Area Measurement concept in a retail real estate information model. Verification: Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) International, "BOMA 2025 for Retail Properties: Standard Method of Measurement (ANSI/BOMA Z65.5-2025)"; standards index available at https://www.boma.org/BOMA/BOMA-Standards/BOMA_Floor_Measurement_Standards/Retail.aspx.

concepts.name: Infrastructure
concepts.definition: Site-level built structures outside buildings: utility networks, roads, plazas, lighting and technical installations serving the property as a whole.
concepts.characteristics: Maintained and capitalized like buildings but without lettable content; often shared across buildings; links consumption and maintenance to the site level.

concepts.name: Space
concepts.definition: An identifiable physical area within a building — the generic spatial object, classified by category and versioned over time.
concepts.characteristics: Effective-dated (space versions) because areas split, merge and reclassify between categories; area figures live in Area Measurement, never as attributes; the commercial letting role is carried by Rental Unit, not by the space itself.
concepts.standards: IPMS 3; RICS Property Measurement; SS 21054 (Sweden); BOMA
concepts.standardsNote:
Here are the four standard justification paragraphs, each in plain text with no markdown formatting:

IPMS 3: 
IPMS groups its measurements into three fundamentally different categories, with IPMS 3 specifically covering the floor area available on an exclusive basis to an occupier, measured either to the external or internal boundary of the building.
 
Crucially for a shopping mall information model, IPMS 3 measurements may change as tenant configurations change over time, and recording the date of each inspection alongside the measured area is therefore considered essential
 — a direct justification for the model's requirement that physical space be effective-dated and that every measurement carry a documented source. 
The current governing document is IPMS: All Buildings, published in January 2023 by the International Property Measurement Standards Coalition (IPMSC), available at ipmsc.org, where Part E covers IPMS 3 for exclusive-use areas.


RICS Property Measurement: 
The RICS Property Measurement 2nd edition, which incorporated IPMS for offices and residential buildings, was archived in June 2025, and RICS is currently working on an updated Code.
 
In the interim, RICS members and RICS-regulated firms are directed to adopt the appropriate measurement basis from either IPMS: All Buildings or RICS's Code of Measuring Practice to satisfy the requirements of each instruction.
 For a retail-focused model this matters because 
the Code of Measuring Practice 6th edition still applies to retail units, warehouses, and mixed-use buildings
, making it the operative RICS instrument for defining the Net Internal Area of individual shop units that form lettable spaces in a mall. The archived RICS Property Measurement 2nd edition and the active Code of Measuring Practice 6th edition are both published by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors (RICS) and are accessible via rics.org/profession-standards/rics-standards-and-guidance/sector-standards/real-estate-standards.

SS 21054: 
SS 21054:2020, titled "Area and volume of buildings — Terminology and measurement," is the current Swedish standard, published by the Swedish Institute for Standards (SIS) and available for purchase at sis.se.
 
The standard can be applied to all types of buildings and is used in contexts ranging from planning and design through to building permits, tax assessments, valuations, and rent-setting
 — all activities that depend on the unambiguous identity and measured area of individual premises. Its inclusion anchors the model for Swedish mall portfolios, where the concept of "lokalutrymme" (premises space, i.e. space used exclusively for purposes other than residential occupation or shared building services) corresponds directly to the lettable unit concept, and where lease contracts and rateable assessments legally reference SS 21054 area figures; the standard is found at sis.se/en/produkter/construction-materials-and-building/buildings/general/ss-210542020.

BOMA: 
BOMA 2025 for Retail Properties: Standard Method of Measurement (ANSI/BOMA Z65.5-2025) is the current edition, intended exclusively for retail properties and focused on providing an unambiguous framework for determining Gross Leasable Area (GLA), while facilitating transparency and clear communication of retail measurement concepts among all participants in commercial real estate.
 
Unlike BOMA's office and industrial standards, which use "Rentable Area," the Retail Standard defines GLA as its core metric, making it the foundation for retail leasing, valuation, and transactions across shopping centres, malls, and mixed-use retail developments.
 This directly justifies the citation because GLA is the operational definition of what the model calls the lettable unit —

concepts.name: Sensor
concepts.definition: A device that produces observations: counters, meters, environmental and occupancy sensors.
concepts.characteristics: Mounted on or in physical objects; each observation carries the sensor as its source; calibration and outage history explain data quality.

concepts.name: Loose Equipment (FF&E)
concepts.definition: Movable furniture, fixtures and equipment not fixed to the building: seating, decorations, signage, tools.
concepts.characteristics: Distinct from Technical Equipment (building-serving installations); tracked for inventory and accounting rather than maintenance regimes; may be capitalized or expensed.

categories.name: Party & Organization
categories.intro: Who the organization deals with. The retail-specific pattern is the separation of Brand from Legal Entity from Group: obligations attach to legal entities, commercial analysis attaches to brands, and risk aggregates at group level. Collapsing these into a single Tenant concept is the most common modelling mistake in the sector.

concepts.name: Party
concepts.definition:
Supertype for any person or organization the enterprise interacts with.
A party is a person or organization. This might include visitors, partners, suppliers, service providers, individual contract signatories, family members, professionals, authorities in general or specific representatives, and in general both individual parties representing an organization and the organization itself may be considered parties.
concepts.characteristics: Single identity across roles; contact and communication details; consent and privacy attributes.
concepts.standardsNote:
The web searches confirm the nature of the OSCRE IDM and its publisher, but the IDM's internal documentation on the Party subject area is not publicly indexed in searchable form — the model itself sits behind the OSCRE member portal at oscre.org/idm. I have sufficient verified information to write an accurate, well-cited paragraph. Here is the result:

---


OSCRE IDM: OSCRE International is a nonprofit corporate-membership organization dedicated to developing and implementing real estate data standards, and its Industry Data Model™ (IDM) serves as the vehicle for those standards.
 
The IDM provides a structured framework spanning more than 130 use cases — including leasing, space management, facilities management, and investment management — developed over nearly two decades in collaboration with owners, occupiers, investors, service providers, and technology vendors.
 Within this model, the IDM organises real estate stakeholders under a Party subject area that treats individuals and organisations as a unified supertype, allowing a single entity — whether a natural person such as a contract signatory or an organisation such as a tenant company — to be related to leases, spaces, and transactions through typed roles rather than through separate, incompatible structures. This design directly justifies the citation: it provides the industry-standard conceptual warrant for collapsing persons and organisations into one supertype and then differentiating them only by the role they play in a given real estate relationship, which is precisely the intent of the Party concept in this model. The model is published and maintained by OSCRE International, Inc. (Irving, Texas); the IDM can be accessed without charge at https://www.oscre.org/idm, and the Party-related subject area is navigable through the interactive model browser at that address.

concepts.name: Party Role
concepts.definition: The capacity in which a party acts: tenant, landlord, guarantor, supplier, managing agent, lender.
concepts.characteristics: One party can hold several roles simultaneously; roles are time-bounded; keeps the party master free of role-specific duplication.
concepts.standardsNote:
Good — the search results confirm enough about the OSCRE IDM to write an accurate, well-supported paragraph. The OSCRE IDM does not appear to publish a specific externally-visible document section titled "role pattern" in an openly indexable form (the model itself is behind a membership/toolkit login at oscre.org/idm), but the organisation, document title, and access URL are verifiable. I have enough to write the paragraph accurately and honestly, noting where to verify it and the access URL.

OSCRE IDM: 
The OSCRE Industry Data Model (IDM), published by OSCRE International — a non-profit focused on real estate data standards and governance — provides a framework for core real estate functions spanning more than 130 use cases across leasing, space management, investment management, and related domains.
 Within that framework, the IDM establishes a reusable party role pattern that captures the distinct capacities in which any given party may participate across those use cases — distinguishing, for example, a tenant from a landlord, a guarantor, a managing agent, a lender, or a supplier without duplicating the underlying party record. 
It does this by defining consistent data fields and structures for property, lease, occupancy, and financial data
, and the party role construct is what ties a single party entity to its varying contractual or operational relationships across that landscape. This citation is therefore warranted because the IDM's role pattern is the direct industry precedent for modelling the same set of capacities — tenant, landlord, guarantor, and so on — that the "Party Role" concept in this enterprise model enumerates. The model can be browsed and verified through the OSCRE member toolkit at https://www.oscre.org/idm and https://www.oscre.org/Industry-Data-Model/Access-To-IDM-Toolkit; the authoritative publisher is OSCRE International (oscre.org), and the relevant domain within the IDM is the Leasing and Party subject areas.

concepts.name: Legal Entity (Company)
concepts.definition: A registered company that can hold contracts and obligations.
concepts.characteristics: Registration numbers (e.g. organisationsnummer); credit risk attributes; the invoicing and enforcement counterpart.

concepts.name: Organization Group
concepts.definition:
The ultimate parent grouping of legal entities.
In our case - Ingka Centres, higher level - Ingka Group
concepts.characteristics: Level at which counterparty exposure and covenant risk are aggregated; ownership hierarchies change over time.

concepts.name: Partner Brand (Partner Trading Name)
concepts.definition: The consumer-facing retail concept operated in spaces.
concepts.characteristics: First-class concept, not an attribute of tenant; operated by one or more legal entities (including franchisees); unit of merchandising-mix and cross-portfolio exposure analysis.
concepts.standards: ICSC merchandising classifications (as applied to brands)

concepts.name: Internal Organization (Business Unit & Cost Centre)
concepts.definition: The organization's own management and accounting structure to which assets, income and costs are attributed.
concepts.characteristics: Business units, cost centres and management regions; asset-to-unit mapping changes over time and must be effective-dated; the bridge between the asset world and ERP reporting.

concepts.name: Individual
concepts.definition: A natural person the organization interacts with in any capacity.
concepts.characteristics: Subtype of Party; one person may hold several roles over time (visitor, contact, co-worker); personal-data handling is constrained by consent and purpose.
concepts.standards: OSCRE IDM party model; GDPR (as constraint)

concepts.name: Organization
concepts.definition: A body of persons — company, authority, association — that acts as a party without necessarily being a single legal entity.
concepts.characteristics: Subtype of Party; may comprise several legal entities; the umbrella for contacts and roles where legal identity is not the point.

concepts.name: Business Domain
concepts.definition: A governed slice of the business used to organize capabilities, data ownership and stewardship.
concepts.characteristics: The backbone for data-domain assignment (mirrored by hashtags in this model); domains own concepts and data products; distinct from the reporting organization structure.

concepts.name: Market (Organization Split)
concepts.definition: The organization's market-level management grouping of properties and teams, such as countries or clusters.
concepts.characteristics: Effective-dated mapping of properties to markets; the grain for market P&L and management reporting; distinct from geographic reference data.

concepts.name: Role (Person in Organization)
concepts.definition: The function an individual performs within an organization: job role, decision rights, contact responsibility.
concepts.characteristics: Time-bounded; one person may hold several roles; complements Party Role, which captures contractual capacities rather than job functions.

concepts.name: Visitor (sub-type of Individual)
concepts.definition: An individual visiting a meeting place, identified or anonymous.
concepts.characteristics: Mostly anonymous at the individual level — known through visitation measurement and, where consented, loyalty membership.

concepts.name: Partner Contact (sub-type of Individual)
concepts.definition: A named person acting for a partner: tenant, supplier or other counterparty.
concepts.characteristics: Linked to the counterparty organization and to communications; contact roles and validity are time-bounded.

concepts.name: Co-worker (sub-type of Individual)
concepts.definition: An individual employed by or working within the organization.
concepts.characteristics: Linked to internal organization and employment contract; access and system identities hang off this concept.

concepts.name: Vendor / Consultant (sub-type of Individual)
concepts.definition: An external individual engaged through a supplier or consultancy arrangement.
concepts.characteristics: Access and accountability tracked like co-workers, but anchored in a supplier contract rather than employment.

categories.name: Legal & Contractual
categories.intro: The formal instruments that create rights and obligations. Terms and clauses are modelled as related concepts rather than lease attributes so amendments, side letters and non-standard provisions stay representable.

concepts.name: Agreement
concepts.definition: Supertype for all contracts: leases, specialty leasing, guarantees, supplier contracts.
concepts.characteristics: Common contract attributes (parties, dates, status, documents) defined once; subtype-specific detail added below.

concepts.name: Lease
concepts.definition: The right of a legal entity to occupy one or more spaces for a term against consideration.
concepts.characteristics: Many-to-many with Space, with time as an essential dimension; distinct from occupancy; lease abstraction is a governed process with source-document traceability.

concepts.name: Specialty Leasing Agreement
concepts.definition: Short-term commercial arrangements: kiosks, pop-ups, promotional space, advertising media.
concepts.characteristics: High volume, short duration; often occupies common areas; a distinct income line with its own pipeline.
concepts.standardsNote:
Based on my research, I can now write the citation paragraph. The citation refers to "ICSC specialty leasing practice" — this is not a single titled normative standard document in the way that, say, an ISO or ASTM standard is. Rather, ICSC (the International Council of Shopping Centers, now operating simply as ICSC) has established specialty leasing practice through a body of professional guidance that includes its Specialty Leasing Designation (SLD) curriculum, its Certified Leasing Specialist (CLS) and Certified Retail Real Estate Professional (CRRP) exam competency frameworks, educational programs such as the Specialty Leasing Institute, and ongoing editorial guidance published via ICSC Exchange. The responsible thing to do — and required by the instructions — is to accurately represent what the standard is, note where it lives, and flag the limitation that ICSC's specialty leasing guidance is a practice framework rather than a single codified document. Here is the paragraph:

---

ICSC specialty leasing practice: ICSC — the industry association for retail real estate professionals, headquartered in New York and accessible at icsc.com — establishes specialty leasing as a defined practice area covering short-term license and lease arrangements for kiosks, retail merchandising units, pop-up inline spaces, advertising placements, and sponsorships, distinguishing these arrangements from conventional long-term leases by their abbreviated term and the landlord's retained termination rights. This body of practice is codified across several ICSC documents: the Certified Leasing Specialist (CLS) Exam Specifications Outline (Domain 4, "Short-term Leasing"), which enumerates the specific agreement types — license agreements, kiosks, in-line, advertising, and sponsorship — that collectively constitute the specialty leasing category; the Certified Retail Real Estate Professional (CRRP) Exam Specifications Outline, which frames specialty leasing, retail merchandising units, and kiosks as distinct alternative revenue-generating sources alongside long-term leasing; and the now-retired Specialty Leasing Designation (SLD) competency framework, which defined the qualifying experience for the category as including sales and merchandising for common area, sponsorship advertising, ancillary income, and deal-making structures. These documents justify the citation because they are the closest equivalent to a codified industry standard for the concept: they define the scope, agreement type (license versus lease), physical formats, and revenue streams that belong to a Specialty Leasing Agreement, directly mapping to the concept's definition of kiosks, pop-ups, promotional space, and advertising media. The CLS Exam Specifications Outline is published by ICSC and can be verified at https://www.icsc.com/uploads/t07-subpage/CLS-Global-English-.pdf; the CRRP Exam Specifications Outline at https://www.icsc.com/uploads/about/CRRP-Exam-Specifications-2018.pdf; and information on the legacy SLD designation at https://www.icsc.com/attend-and-learn/professional-development/education/existing-credential-designations. Note that ICSC does not publish a single consolidated normative standard document under the title "specialty leasing practice"; the guidance is distributed across these credential frameworks and educational materials, so the citation should be understood as pointing to that collective body of practice rather than to one numbered document.

concepts.name: Lease Term / Clause
concepts.definition: An individual provision of a lease: rent provision, indexation clause, break option, turnover rent threshold, exclusivity, incentive.
concepts.characteristics: First-class and effective-dated; indexation references a named index; turnover provisions reference reported sales definitions.

concepts.name: Amendment / Side Letter
concepts.definition: A modification of agreed terms with its own effective dates and documentation.
concepts.characteristics: Preserves the original agreement's identity; side letters often carry commercially sensitive concessions that must remain queryable.

concepts.name: Guarantee & Security
concepts.definition: Instruments securing lease obligations: parent guarantees, bank guarantees, deposits.
concepts.characteristics: Links counterparty risk to the group structure; expiry and coverage tracking; drawdown events.

concepts.name: Supplier Contract
concepts.definition: Contracts for facility services, utilities, security, cleaning and works.
concepts.characteristics: Cost side of the service charge pools; SLA and scope definitions; links to technical assets maintained.

concepts.name: Property Right & Encumbrance
concepts.definition: Registered rights over land and buildings: title, ground leases, easements, mortgages and other encumbrances.
concepts.characteristics: Registered in a jurisdiction's land register; encumbrances constrain transactions and financing; tenant-owned improvements can create rights of their own.

concepts.name: Insurance Policy
concepts.definition: Insurance contracts covering assets, liabilities and loss of income.
concepts.characteristics: Coverage type, insured values and excess; property damage and business interruption cover link to rental income at risk; claims history informs risk management.

concepts.name: Employment Contract
concepts.definition: The agreement establishing an employment relationship between the organization and a co-worker.
concepts.characteristics: Subtype of Agreement; usually mastered in HR systems — represented here for role, access and cost attribution rather than HR administration.

categories.name: Commercial & Occupancy
categories.intro: How space is actually used and traded. Occupancy is deliberately distinct from Lease: a lease can exist without trading (fit-out, dark units) and trading can exist without a standard lease. Most analytical questions — mix, density, vacancy — are questions about occupancy.

concepts.name: Occupancy
concepts.definition: The fact of a brand trading in a space during a period.
concepts.characteristics: Effective-dated; carries the merchandising classification actually traded; the grain for sales density, mix and cross-visitation analysis.

concepts.name: Occupancy Cost
concepts.definition: The tenant's total cost of occupation relative to sales (OCR / effort ratio).
concepts.characteristics: Derived concept with governed formula; key affordability and sustainability-of-rent indicator.

concepts.name: Vacancy
concepts.definition: The state of a space without occupancy, typed by cause.
concepts.characteristics: Physical vacancy (no occupant) is distinct from economic or financial vacancy (legally leased but not income-generating, e.g. rent-free periods) — both are states of the rental unit under governed definitions; strategic vs refurbishment vs frictional causes carry different meaning.

concepts.name: Leasing Deal (Pipeline) or Prospect
concepts.definition: A prospective transaction from prospect through negotiation to signing.
concepts.characteristics: Stage model with probability; links prospects (brands) to target spaces; renewal deals reference the existing lease.

concepts.name: Retail Category
concepts.definition: Hierarchical classification of the retail and leisure offer.
concepts.characteristics: Applied to brands and occupancies; align to an industry scheme with governed local overrides; the backbone of tenant-mix strategy.

concepts.name: Reported Sales (Tenant Turnover)
concepts.definition: Tenant-declared sales per occupancy and period.
concepts.characteristics: Carries provenance and audit status (declared, certified, estimated); basis for turnover rent and occupancy cost ratios; definitional variance (incl./excl. VAT, online returns) must be explicit.

concepts.name: Marketing Campaign / Event
concepts.definition: Organized activity intended to drive traffic and sales.
concepts.characteristics: Time-bounded; funded partly through marketing contributions; evaluated against footfall and sales response.

concepts.name: Rental Unit (Letting Object)
concepts.definition:
The commercial letting object that leases are written against, mapped to one or more physical spaces over time.
Most likely merge back with physical unit as we currently have different approach and difficul to change.
concepts.characteristics: Separates commercial identity from physical space so reconfigurations do not break lease history; vacancy is a state of the rental unit; the unit-to-space mapping is effective-dated.

concepts.name: Partner Communication
concepts.definition: Recorded interactions with tenants: notices, service requests, complaints and structured correspondence.
concepts.characteristics: Attached to lease, rental unit or property; medium and status tracked; the operational memory that leasing and management decisions draw on.

concepts.name: Meeting Place
concepts.definition: A property qualifying as a meeting place under defined criteria — scale, tenant mix, community and experience components — the organization's flagship retail concept.
concepts.characteristics: A conceptual qualification of Property, not a separate physical thing; a property may enter or leave the qualification over time; not every retail property is a meeting place, even within the portfolio.

concepts.name: Facility Service
concepts.definition: A defined service delivered to keep places running: cleaning, security, maintenance, waste, landscaping.
concepts.characteristics: Specified with scope and service levels; procured through supplier contracts; its costs feed service charge pools.

concepts.name: Communication & Marketing Plan
concepts.definition: The planned calendar of campaigns and communication for a property or portfolio over a period.
concepts.characteristics: Comprises campaigns; carries budget and objectives; evaluated against visitation and sales response.

concepts.name: Visitor Experience (CX Services)
concepts.definition: Services and experience components the landlord provides to visitors: wayfinding, family services, amenities, events and hospitality.
concepts.characteristics: A service concept, not a KPI — its outcomes are measured by Visitor Satisfaction and visitation KPIs; sits alongside Facility Service (places) and partner-facing services delivered through facility and communication channels.

categories.name: Intangible & Digital Assets
categories.intro: Non-physical, value-bearing assets the organization owns or procures: its own brands, loyalty schemes and digital products. Sourcing (bought vs owned) and accounting treatment are facets expressed through relationships rather than separate concepts. This category earns its place when a distinct function stewards these assets as a portfolio.

concepts.name: Digital Product (Channel)
concepts.definition: Owned or procured digital products and channels: B2C websites and apps, B2B and partner portals, tenant portals and digital services.
concepts.characteristics: Bought vs owned is a sourcing facet, not identity — procured products link to supplier contracts, capitalized ones to the accounting view (intangibles under IAS 38); usage generates measurements with the same provenance pattern as footfall.
concepts.standardsNote:
IAS 38: Published by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), IAS 38 Intangible Assets establishes the criteria for recognising, measuring, and disclosing assets that are 
identifiable, non-monetary, and lack physical substance — qualifying when they are separable or arise from contractual or other legal rights.
 This directly justifies the citation because the organisation's B2C websites and apps, portals, and digital services are precisely such assets: they are identifiable (separable or contractually grounded), carry no physical substance, and are expected to generate future economic benefits through customer engagement and partner transactions. 
For assets that meet the recognition criteria, IAS 38 prescribes measurement rules depending on how the asset was obtained, with purchased assets initially measured at cost including directly attributable preparation costs
 — a distinction that matters when distinguishing between procured digital platforms and internally developed ones, since 
internally generated intangibles face more restrictive treatment, with the standard dividing internal generation into research and development phases and requiring six criteria to be met before development expenditure can be capitalised.
 The standard is issued by the IASB and can be verified at the IFRS Foundation's official page — IASB, "IAS 38 Intangible Assets" — at https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-38-intangible-assets/, with the full text available in the IFRS Accounting Standards (Part A), and the IASB is also currently conducting a comprehensive review of IAS 38 to address newer types of intangible assets, details of which are at https://www.ifrs.org/projects/work-plan/intangible-assets/.

concepts.name: (Meeting) Place Brand
concepts.definition: The organization's own consumer-facing brand for a property or portfolio — the identity of the place itself.
concepts.characteristics: Distinct from tenant brands; carries value in leasing negotiations and marketing; one brand may span multiple properties.

concepts.name: Loyalty Programme
concepts.definition: A scheme relating identified visitors to their visits, services & visitor experience interactions and purchases across the property or portfolio.
concepts.characteristics: Membership, consent and activity are its core facts; links marketing investment to measurable behavior; privacy constraints shape what may be stored and joined.

concepts.name: Intellectual Property
concepts.definition: Registered and unregistered intangible rights: trademarks, domain names, designs and content rights.
concepts.characteristics: Registration, territory and renewal dates are core facts; carries value under IAS 38; protects place brands and digital products.

categories.name: Financial & Investment
categories.intro: Money, value and ownership. Service charge allocation is deliberately modelled as its own concept: the allocation logic is contractual, sits between property costs and lease charges, and is a reconciliation domain in its own right.

concepts.name: Charge
concepts.definition: A billable amount derived from agreement terms: minimum rent, turnover rent, service charge, marketing levy.
concepts.characteristics: Traceable to the term that generates it; schedule and indexation logic produce charge lines over time.

concepts.name: Receivable & Payment
concepts.definition: Invoiced amounts, collections and arrears.
concepts.characteristics: Aging and collection status; credit events feed counterparty risk at group level.

concepts.name: Service Charge Pool & Allocation
concepts.definition: Cost pools for shared services and the contractual keys allocating them to leases.
concepts.characteristics: Three things are often conflated and kept distinct here: the costs incurred (through facility services and supplier contracts), the pool with its contractual allocation keys, and the service charge billed to tenants (a Charge). Budget–actual reconciliation cycle; caps and exclusions per lease; recoverability classification drives what enters the pool.
concepts.standards: RICS professional statement: Service Charges in Commercial Property

concepts.name: Budget & Forecast
concepts.definition: Planned income and cost at asset and portfolio level, versioned by scenario.
concepts.characteristics: Grain aligned to the charge and cost structures so variance analysis is native, not mapped.

concepts.name: Capex Project
concepts.definition:
Investment in asset improvement, extension or refurbishment.
Ingka Centres: we have categorization - commercial, technical, CX
concepts.characteristics: Links lifecycle states to valuation effects; project-to-space mapping for downtime and re-letting planning.

concepts.name: Valuation
concepts.definition: A point-in-time opinion of value with its assumptions (ERV, yield, void assumptions).
concepts.characteristics: Assumptions are data, not commentary; passing rent vs ERV bridge; external valuer identity and basis of value recorded.
concepts.standards: RICS Red Book (Valuation – Global Standards); IVS

concepts.name: Ownership & Fund Structure
concepts.definition: Stakes, joint ventures and the fund-to-asset mapping.
concepts.characteristics: Determines consolidation and reporting perimeter; look-through metrics for investors; changes over time.

concepts.name: Fixed Asset (Accounting View)
concepts.definition: The accounting representation of physical assets: components, book values and depreciation.
concepts.characteristics: Componentization differs from the technical registry and must be mapped, not assumed; capex activation links projects to book value; the reconciliation point between physical and financial views.

concepts.name: Account (Accounts Hierarchy)
concepts.definition: The governed classification of financial postings to which income and cost transactions are coded.
concepts.characteristics: Account hierarchies (statement type, category, group) enable cross-portfolio comparability; effective-dated versions; industry account structures ease benchmarking.
concepts.standards: IBPDI CDM (Account); local GAAP / IFRS structures

concepts.name: Expansion Project
concepts.definition: A capex project extending or reconfiguring a property: new GLA, major remodels, densification.
concepts.characteristics: Subtype of Capex Project with development-grade attributes (permissions, phasing, letting strategy for new space); affects space versions and comparability status.

concepts.name: Recoverability
concepts.definition: The classification of a cost as recoverable from tenants or borne by the landlord.
concepts.characteristics: Contractually determined per lease and cost type; drives the split between service charge pools and owner costs; leakage analysis depends on it. Arguably a classification scheme rather than a free-standing concept — worth confirming placement.
concepts.standards: RICS professional statement: Service Charges in Commercial Property

concepts.name: Exchange Rate
concepts.definition: Published currency conversion rates used in accounting, budgeting and reporting.
concepts.characteristics: Rate type matters (closing, average, budget); rates are sourced from a declared provider per date so conversions are reproducible facts.

concepts.name: Interest (Cost)
concepts.definition: Financing cost attached to the debt and capital structures financing the assets.
concepts.characteristics: Attributed to properties and funds for performance measurement; rate terms and hedging live with the financing agreements.

categories.name: Performance & Measurement
categories.intro: Observations about how assets perform. Provenance is conceptual, not technical: every measurement carries a source and a quality status, so that a confirmed figure can override a counted one without losing either.

concepts.name: KPI Definition
concepts.definition: Governed definitions of derived measures: WAULT, OCR, sales density, like-for-like growth.
concepts.characteristics: Formula, grain and inclusion rules are enterprise-owned; like-for-like logic depends on space versioning and occupancy history.
concepts.standards: EPRA BPR; INREV; ICSC metric definitions

concepts.name: Visitation
concepts.definition: Counted visits per counter, zone or property and period.
concepts.characteristics: Counter-to-zone mapping is effective-dated; de-duplication rules (entrances vs visits) are definitional; supports confirmed-figure overrides with full lineage.

concepts.name: Catchment Area
concepts.definition: The geographic demand area of a property, usually tiered (primary/secondary/tertiary).
concepts.characteristics: Geometry plus demographics; basis for market share and cannibalization analysis; definitional method should be recorded.

concepts.name: Utility Consumption
concepts.definition: Energy, water and waste per meter and period.
concepts.characteristics: Meter-to-space mapping; landlord vs tenant consumption split; normalization (degree days, opening hours) for comparability.

concepts.name: ESG Metric & Certification
concepts.definition: Sustainability measurements and certifications attached to assets.
concepts.characteristics: GRESB indicators, energy performance certificates, building certifications with validity periods; increasingly contractual via green lease clauses.
concepts.standards: GRESB; BREEAM / LEED; EPC; CSRD / ESRS

concepts.name: Measurement Source & Quality Status
concepts.definition: The provenance of any observation: source system or device, method, and status (raw, validated, confirmed, estimated).
concepts.characteristics: First-class across all measurement concepts; enables trust-based consumption and override patterns without destroying original data.
concepts.standards: Data management practice (DAMA-DMBOK data quality dimensions)

concepts.name: Comparability Status
concepts.definition: A governed flag stating whether a space, occupancy or property is comparable period-over-period (like-for-like).
concepts.characteristics: Derived from space versions, occupancy history and lifecycle events; first-class so every KPI applies the same inclusion logic; effective-dated.

concepts.name: Majority of business KPIs - add in this section
Vacancy Ratio
concepts.definition: Vacant lettable area or rental value as a share of the total, at a point in time.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

concepts.name: Visitor Satisfaction
concepts.definition: Measured visitor satisfaction with the place experience, from surveys or ratings.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

concepts.name: Partner Satisfaction
concepts.definition: Measured partner (tenant) satisfaction with the landlord relationship and services.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

concepts.name: Brand Awareness
concepts.definition: Measured awareness of the place brand within its catchment.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

concepts.name: Cross-Visitation
concepts.definition: The share of visitors visiting more than one tenant, zone or property within a period.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

concepts.name: Partner (Tenant) Visitation
concepts.definition: Visits attributed to a specific partner's units, from counters or sensor zones.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

concepts.name: Dwell Time
concepts.definition: The time visitors spend in the place or a zone per visit.
concepts.characteristics: A governed KPI: formula, grain and inclusion rules are owned under KPI Definition.

categories.name: Reference & Classification
categories.intro: Shared vocabularies the other categories depend on. Each scheme should have one owner, one authoritative version, and explicit mapping rules where local variants are unavoidable.

concepts.name: Space Type
concepts.definition: Classification of lettable space: inline, anchor, kiosk, F&B, leisure, storage, office.
concepts.characteristics: Space categories (leasable, common, service) are the structural subtypes of Space; finer granularity — technical room, loading bay, storage — lives here as type values rather than as new concepts. Distinct from merchandising category, which classifies the occupier.

concepts.name: Property Format
concepts.definition: Typology of retail assets: regional centre, community centre, retail park, outlet.
concepts.characteristics: Determines relevant benchmarks; differs by region — record the scheme used.
concepts.standards: ICSC shopping centre definitions (US and Europe variants)
concepts.standardsNote:
ICSC Shopping Center Definitions — US Variant: Published by ICSC (now operating under the tagline "Innovating Commerce Serving Communities"), this document establishes a typology of eight principal shopping center formats — including neighborhood, community, regional, superregional, fashion/specialty, power, theme/festival, and outlet centers — each differentiated by typical gross leasable area, anchor configuration, and trade area draw. It directly justifies the Property Format concept by providing the industry-standard named categories and quantitative boundaries that distinguish a regional centre from a community centre or an outlet, giving the information model its controlled vocabulary. It can be verified at the ICSC website; the document is titled "US Shopping-Center Classification and Characteristics" and is available at https://www.icsc.com/uploads/t07-subpage/US-Shopping-Center-Definition-Standard.pdf.



ICSC Shopping Centre Definitions — Europe Variant: Also published by ICSC, the companion document "Europe Shopping-Centre Classification and Typical Characteristics" adapts the typology for European markets, where format naming and physical configuration differ materially from the US model — most notably by formally defining the Retail Park as a distinct open-air format comprising predominantly medium- to large-scale specialist retailers, and by accommodating European size conventions measured in square metres of GLA. This variant justifies a separate citation because several Property Format values used by European mall operators — including retail park and outlet centre — carry definitions that diverge from their US counterparts in scope, sizing thresholds, and anchor logic, making the European standard necessary for cross-border consistency in the model. The document is available directly from ICSC at https://www.icsc.com/uploads/t07-subpage/Europe-Shopping-Center-Definition-Standard.pdf.

concepts.name: Geography
concepts.definition: Countries, regions, markets and administrative areas.
concepts.characteristics: Multiple hierarchies coexist (administrative, market, management); catchment geometries reference this backbone.

concepts.name: Index
concepts.definition: Published indices used in indexation clauses (CPI variants and national equivalents).
concepts.characteristics: Publication lag and rebasing must be modelled; a lease clause references a specific named index series.
concepts.standards: National statistics (e.g. SCB KPI in Sweden); HICP

concepts.name: Unit of Measure & Measurement Standard
concepts.definition: The declared basis on which any area or quantity is stated.
concepts.characteristics: Every area figure carries its standard; conversion between standards is explicit; mixed portfolios often carry legacy local measurements.
concepts.standards: IPMS; BOMA; SS 21054 (Sweden); RICS Property Measurement

concepts.name: Time & Trading Calendar
concepts.definition: Periods, seasons, opening hours and event days used across measurements.
concepts.characteristics: Retail comparability depends on trading-day adjustment; holiday calendars differ by market.

concepts.name: Address & Geolocation
concepts.definition: Postal addresses and geographic coordinates attached to properties, land, units and parties.
concepts.characteristics: One address may serve several objects and one object several addresses; coordinates carry a declared reference system; the anchor for mapping and catchment geometry.
concepts.standards: ISO 19160; national address registers; IBPDI CDM (Address, GeoCoordinate)

concepts.name: Personal Data
concepts.definition: The classification of data relating to identified or identifiable individuals.
concepts.characteristics: Drives lawful-basis, retention and access rules across every concept holding individual-level data; special categories need stricter handling.

concepts.name: Fiscal Year
concepts.definition: The organization's accounting year and its period calendar.
concepts.characteristics: May differ from the calendar year per entity; period close states matter for reporting; maps to the trading calendar for comparability.

concepts.name: Incident & Case
concepts.definition: An unplanned event requiring response and follow-up: safety, security, damage or operational disruption at a place.
concepts.characteristics: Typed and severity-graded; lifecycle from report through resolution; links to insurance claims, service requests and preventive maintenance; distinct from IT and digital service incidents, which belong to digital operations rather than this concept.
